checks.finding: All models fall far below the conventional EPV>=10 threshold. Discovery 3-pathway EPV=1.0-1.33; even single-feature discovery EPV=4.0; BriTROC single-feature EPV=3.0 (3 resistant). High overfitting/instability risk; all estimates discovery-grade.
checks.verdict: SUPPORTED (manuscript discloses low EPV; quantified here)

checks.finding: With only 3 resistant patients, removing a single resistant case swings the s7-relapse AUROC materially (LORO range shown). The 0.874 headline is highly unstable.
checks.verdict: OVERSTATED (point estimate presented with insufficient emphasis on n=3 fragility)

checks.finding: Discovery AUCs (post_pi3k 0.750, post_ddr 0.714) and correlations are APPARENT (full-sample, no CV, no bootstrap CI). With n=11 these are optimistic and lack uncertainty bounds. Manuscript discloses this explicitly.
checks.verdict: SUPPORTED (disclosed) but headline framing should always pair with 'apparent, n=11'

checks.finding: Applying BH-FDR across the 7 discovery tests: 6 survive at FDR<0.05. Manuscript applied NO correction. Even the strongest signals should be read as hypothesis-generating after correction.
checks.verdict: OVERSTATED (no MT correction applied; some p-values weaken under FDR)

checks.finding: Kaplan-Meier stratification uses the median computed from the SAME n=11 data used for discovery. This is data leakage; the log-rank p (0.0124) is optimistic. A prespecified/external threshold is required. Manuscript discloses this.
checks.verdict: SUPPORTED (disclosed leakage) - keep as limitation, not a headline

checks.finding: AUROC 0.874 and 0.750 are discrimination metrics on tiny cohorts; they are NOT clinical-utility evidence. No calibration, no decision-curve analysis, no prespecified threshold, no net-benefit. Prognostic association != predictive clinical utility.
